'''J. S. R. (Roy) Chisholm''' (26 November 1926 – 10 August 2015) was an English [[mathematical physicist]]. He was Professor Emeritus of Applied Mathematics at the [[University of Kent]] in [[Canterbury]], where he worked from its founding in 1965 until 1994. Before that he held positions at the [[University of Glasgow]] (1951-1954) and Cardiff (1954-1962) following which he was appointed Dublin University [[Professor of Natural Philosophy at Trinity College Dublin]] (1962-1966).<ref>[https://www.maths.tcd.ie/about/400Hist/7.php University Professors of Natural Philosophy at TCD 1592–1992]</ref>  He held BA (1948) and PhD (1952) degrees from Cambridge.<ref>[https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/outreach-initiatives/summa/summa-archival-record/william-claytor J. S. Roy Chisholm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191215192911/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/outreach-initiatives/summa/summa-archival-record/william-claytor |date=15 December 2019 }} at the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA)</ref><ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=84654 J. S. Roy Chisholm] at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref><ref>[https://www.iop.org/about/obituaries/page_72170.html#gref Obiturary:  John (“Roy”) Chisholm (1926-2015)] Institute of Physics</ref>

Chisholm developed a method for rational approximations of two variable functions generalising [[Padé approximant]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Chisholm|first=J. S. R.|date=1973|title=Rational approximants defined from double power series|url=https://www.ams.org/mcom/1973-27-124/S0025-5718-1973-0382928-6/|journal=Mathematics of Computation|volume=27|issue=124|pages=841–848|doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-1973-0382928-6|issn=0025-5718|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Roy Chisholm initiated the first International Conference on Clifford Algebras and Their Applications in Mathematical Physics (ICCA) conference in 1985 which took place  at the [[University of Kent]] in Canterbury, United Kingdom, and which has happened triennially since then. 

He was married to [[Monty Chisholm]], author of a book on English literary figure wife [[Lucy Clifford]] and mathematician husband [[William Kingdon Clifford]].<ref>{{cite book
|last=Chisholm
|first=Monty
|title=Such Silver Currents: The Story of William and Lucy Clifford, 1845-1929
|year=2002
|publisher=James Clarke & Co Ltd
|location=Cambridge
|isbn=9780718830175
|edition=Paperback
}}</ref>



==Books==
*''An Introduction to Statistical Mechanics'', with A.H.de Borde, Pergamon Press (1958)
*''Mathematical Methods in Physics'', with [[Rosa M. Morris|Rosa Morris]], North-Holland (1964)
*''[[Vectors in three-dimensional space|Vectors in Three-Dimensional Space]]'' (Cambridge University Press,1978)
*''Clifford Algebras and Their Applications in Mathematical Physics'', co-edited with A.K.Common (Reidel 1986)
*''Clifford Analysis and its Applications'', co-eds F.Brackx & V.Soucek (Kluwer 2001)
*Changing Stations, a Campus Drama (Moat Sole 2014)
